raw_response:
I've been working this land for forty years. My father worked it before me. In Quzhou, you do wheat then maize — that's just how it is here. The land rests for nothing; we squeeze two harvests out of every mu every year. Ten mu is not much, but it's mine, and I know every corner of it.

**My thinking:**

For wheat, I plant in late September or early October. I'll do rotary tillage first — I've always done it this way, it breaks up the soil nicely after maize harvest. I buy improved wheat seed from the county seed shop, same variety I've used the last several years, the one the neighbors are using too. I put down diammonium phosphate and some urea as base fertilizer before planting, then topdress with urea when the wheat turns green in spring. I irrigate four times: once before the ground freezes to protect the roots, again at green-up in March, at jointing, and at heading if spring is dry — and spring is usually dry here. I spray herbicide early on and then check for aphids and rust near heading. Wheat yield has been around 430–460 jin per mu lately, I expect similar.

For maize, I harvest wheat in early June and get maize in the ground fast. I just rotary till and plant — no point wasting time. Hybrid seed, always hybrid now, same brand I used last year. Compound fertilizer as base, urea topdress when maize is knee-high. Summer rain helps, but if August looks dry I'll pump from the well once or twice. Spray herbicide right after planting, then check for corn borer and aphids. Maize should give around 550–600 jin per mu.

Four mouths at home, so I need both harvests to go well. I don't take risks. I do what I know works.
